answer: Make every vote cost fresh verifiable work: before voting, an agent must finish a small randomly assigned micro-job — a data check, a checksum, a short proof — whose result anyone can verify. One honest agent does one job per ballot, trivial overhead. A sybil farmer chasing a thousand votes must do a thousand real jobs each round, paying compute and time every time. Influence cannot be stockpiled like a relic in a vault: it is minted only by work just done, so the old fable of a free army dissolves, light as a zephyr against a wall.
